The '''All Terrain Attack Pod (AT-AP)''', or '''Pod Attack Walker (PAW)''',<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> was a tripedal [[Walker/Legends|walker]] that evolved from the [[All Terrain Personal Transport/Legends|AT-PT]] and [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]] walkers towards the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. They were used by the [[327th Star Corps/Legends|327th Star Corps]], [[91st Mobile Reconnaissance Corps/Legends|91st Reconnaissance Corps]], [[41st Stormtrooper Legion|41st Elite Corps]], [[282nd Regiment]], [[121st Regiment]], [[96th Regiment]], [[76th Regiment]], [[212th Attack Battalion/Legends|212th Attack Battalion]], among other units in [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] and [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial army]].<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank">{{DB|vehicle|atap|All Terrain Attack Pod (AT-AP walker)}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
[[File:Atapkashyyyk.jpg|thumb|left|180px|AT-APs on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].]]
The AT-AP (All Terrain Attack Pod) was conceived as a means of transporting a piece of heavy artillery across the battlefront. Its main function was to serve as a mobile gun platform used for shelling enemy positions, rather than attacking troops or other vehicles. It featured highly-advanced targeting systems that led to it being nicknamed the "sniper tank." Although classified as a two-legged walker, the AT-AP did have a third leg hanging from underneath the fuselage designed to help stabilize the walker. It would extend and deploy at the operator's discretion: typically when overcoming rough terrain or firing its main gun.<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank" />

The AT-AP was armed with a [[Mass-driver cannon/Legends|mass-driver cannon]] fixed to the front of the craft, a heavy [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannon]] mounted on a turret (which had an open-cockpit, making the gunner susceptible to enemy infantry fire), and a medium [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] at the bottom of the main fuselage.<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank" /> Behind the main weapon's [[Gunner/Legends|gunner's]] saddle was a supply cage filled with tools necessary for repairing any mechanical failure to the walker's articulation assembly.<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank" />

==History==
===The Clone Wars===
As the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] raged on, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|army]] [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] recognized a need to build up and diversify their walker armor.<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank" /> One of the new designs that emerged from the Republic's think-tanks was the AT-AP, an artillery walker based off the fore compartment of the [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]].<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank" />

<div style="float:right">[[File:AT-AP_sideview.jpg|thumb|180px|AT-AP profile.]]</div>
Although armored, the AT-AP was too specialized to be used on its own in direct combat. It and other gun batteries of this type would usually be accompanied by heavier equipment, such as AT-TEs, [[Unstable Terrain Artillery Transport/Legends|Tridents]] and [[HAVw A6 Juggernaut/Legends|HAVw A6 Juggernauts]] on the battlefield.<ref name="AT-AP in the Databank" /> In the waning days of the Clone Wars, the AT-AP found extensive use in multiple Outer Rim theaters.

A great number of these walkers were attached to the [[41st Stormtrooper Legion|41st Elite Corps]] in the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]], where they helped defend the city of [[Kachirho/Legends|Kachirho]] alongside the A6 Juggernaut.<ref name="ROTS" /> They found similar application on planets like [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]] and [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]], the former under the command of [[Stass Allie/Legends|Stass Allie]] and the latter with [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] alongside [[All Terrain Open Transport/Legends|AT-OTs]] and [[Infantry Support Platform/Legends|ISPs]].<ref name="ROTS" />

===Later use===
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], some of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] AT-APs were manufactured by formerly abandoned factories out on the fringe, leading to [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] forces hijacking lines and getting some of the walkers.<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>

Some AT-APs also fell into the hands of [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]], and other groups such as the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]], leading to skirmishes and outright battles against either Rebels or Imperials. Hutt Palaces were also known to keep the walkers among their stocks of Clone Wars surplus.<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>

AT-APs saw extensive use on Kashyyyk, fighting alongside [[All Terrain Kashyyyk Transport|AT-KTs]] in the ongoing conflict with [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] insurgents.<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
LEGO has released three versions of the AT-AP Walker with green markings in 2008, 2014, and, most recently, in 2019, with set numbers 7671, 75043, and 75234 respectively.

The AT-AP was also the first "Air Support" vehicle to be available in 2011's Lego Star Wars III: The Clone Wars video game.
